title: Space Days Out for Kids: Rockets, Planetariums and More
description: Space days out for kids and teens: the National Space Centre, Royal Observatory Greenwich, Science Museum, Kennedy Space Center and planetarium shows.
h1: Space days out for kids and teens
intro: Rockets, astronauts and the universe on a dome above your head. These are the best days out for space-mad kids and teens.

image.alt: Two adults and a child looking out at a mountain view

cardText: Space centres, planetariums and real rockets.

blocks.title: Scout’s space tip
blocks.text: Planetarium shows have set times and limited seats. Book or grab tickets as soon as you arrive.

sections.html:
• National Space Centre, Leicester: rockets, galleries and a planetarium.
  • Royal Observatory Greenwich: the Prime Meridian and the Peter Harrison Planetarium.
  • Science Museum, London: free space galleries.

Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex in Florida has real rockets and the Space Shuttle Atlantis, an easy add-on to an Orlando trip. The Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum in Washington, DC is free.
Head outside after dark: see stargazing with kids. Browse museums and science.

faqs.q: Is the Science Museum space gallery free?
faqs.a: General admission to the Science Museum is free, including its permanent space galleries. Some exhibitions and experiences charge.
